content.text: spasticity: escalating doses of baclofen or tizanidine; botulinum toxin injections if oral tx fails.

Titrate: 5 mg t.i.d. 3 days, 10 mg t.i.d. 3 days, 15 mg t.i.d. 3 days, 20 mg t.i.d. 3 days. Start low and ↑ gradually until optimum effect (usually 40 to 80 mg daily). Max total daily dose 80 mg (20 mg q.i.d.). Lowest dose compatible w optimal response recommended; slowly withdraw if no benefit after a reasonable trial.

CI: hypersensitivity to baclofen. Hallucinations and seizures have occurred on abrupt withdrawal — reduce dose slowly when discontinuing. Primarily excreted unchanged by kidneys — give w caution; may be necessary to reduce the dosage. Neonatal withdrawal (↑ muscle tone, tremor, jitteriness, seizure) reported hours to days after delivery in neonates of mothers treated throughout pregnancy.

Sedation possible — caution w driving/machinery; CNS effects may be additive to alcohol and other CNS depressants. Epilepsy: monitor clinical state and EEG at regular intervals (deterioration in seizure control/EEG reported occasionally).

OD signs: vomiting, muscular hypotonia, drowsiness, accommodation disorders, coma, respiratory depression, seizures. OD tx: empty stomach (emesis then lavage) if alert; if obtunded secure airway w cuffed endotracheal tube b4 lavage (do not induce emesis); maintain respiratory exchange; do not use respiratory stimulants.

Start 2 mg PO every 6 to 8 h as needed, max three doses in 24 h. ↑ by 2 mg to 4 mg per dose every 1 to 4 days; max total daily dose 36 mg. Renal impairment (CrCl <25 mL/min) or hepatic impairment: use lower individual doses during titration; ↑ individual doses rather than frequency. Monitor aminotransferase levels at baseline and 1 month after max dose is achieved.
strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. CI: Hx of hypersensitivity to tizanidine or ingredients (anaphylaxis, angioedema).

Hypotension risk minimized by dose titration; monitor for hypotension signs/symptoms prior to dosage increase. Monitor for hypotension w concurrent antihypertensive therapy. May cause liver injury — monitor ALTs; discontinue if liver injury occurs. CNS depressant effects w alcohol and other CNS depressants (e.g., benzodiazepines, opioids, tricyclic antidepressants) may be additive. May cause hallucinations — consider discontinuing Zanaflex. Withdrawal (rebound hypertension, tachycardia, hypertonia): decrease dose slowly, esp after high doses (20 to 28 mg daily) for long periods (9 weeks or more) or w narcotics.

Strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin) ↑ tizanidine exposure — significantly ↓ BP, ↑ drowsiness, ↑ psychomotor impairment. OD: ↓ sensorium (lethargy, somnolence, confusion, coma), depressed cardiac function (most often bradycardia, hypotension), respiratory depression.
